policies.title: New Zealand and Saudi ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Ukraine's current Presidential Decree No. 289/2020 grants New Zealand and Saudi citizens visa-free entry and transit for short stays of up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The decree covers entry into Ukraine and transit by citizens of New Zealand and Saudi Arabia for no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
This is the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline; it does not establish work, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Republic of Korea ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The Republic of Korea Foreign Ministry's live Ukraine entry panel marks ordinary Republic of Korea passports visa-free for an aggregate 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The live Korean Foreign Ministry entry panel expressly marks ordinary Republic of Korea passports eligible without a visa for 90 days in the preceding 180 days.

The same source identifies Ukraine as subject to a Korean domestic travel prohibition/permission rule. That operational rule is a condition on Korean travel, not a published Ukrainian suspension of the visa waiver.
This is the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline; it does not establish employment, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Ukraine-Brunei agreement exempts Brunei citizens using valid foreign-travel passports from visas for entry, transit, exit, and stays of up to 30 days.
conditions: The agreement applies to citizens using valid passports for travel abroad and permits entry, transit, exit, and a visa-free stay of up to 30 days.

A stay exceeding 30 days requires a visa before entry under the agreement. This policy does not establish employment, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Marshall Islands ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Ukraine-Marshall Islands agreement expressly includes normal Marshall Islands passports and waives visas for entry, stay, exit, and transit up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The annex expressly lists a normal Marshall Islands passport, while Article 1 permits visa-free entry, stay, exit, and transit for up to 90 days in 180 days.

A stay exceeding 90 days requires a visa before entry regardless of purpose. This policy does not establish employment, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Belarusian ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Ukraine-Belarus agreement retains visa-free travel for a Belarusian citizen passport up to 90 days in 180 days; Ukraine's 2020 partial suspension concerned only the Ukrainian domestic-passport subpoint.
conditions: The current agreement lists the passport of a citizen of Belarus, grants visa-free travel, and caps stays at 90 days in 180 days from first entry.
Resolution No. 362/2020 suspends only Appendix subpoint 1.1, identified in the consolidated agreement as the Ukrainian domestic passport; it does not suspend the Belarusian ordinary-passport route.
This is the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline; it does not establish employment, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Armenian ordinary passports: Ukraine visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current Ukraine-Armenia agreement covers the Armenian citizen passport for visa-free entry, transit, exit, and stay; Ukraine's current general visa-free calculation is 90 days in 180 days where the agreement sets no different term.
conditions: The agreement covers the passport of a citizen of Armenia for visa-free entry, exit, transit, and stay. It does not specify a different stay duration.
The current State Migration Service rule therefore limits the visa-free stay to 90 days in 180 days unless an international agreement supplies another term.
This is the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline; it does not establish employment, residence, special-document, carrier, security, border-access, or final-admission treatment.

unresolved.reason: Presidential Decree No. 1107/2005 directly states a visa waiver for Japanese citizens, but its live official record does not affirmatively label the decree in force. Current legal force is not established to this batch's strict standard.

The nationality-specific MFA page that could corroborate current implementation returned HTTP 403 when replayed, and its June 2023 table cannot be used alone. A current ordinary Azerbaijani-passport visitor baseline is not established.
